extra.message: The 'searchText' parameter is concatenated directly into a SQL query string passed to db.all(), with no parameterization (a parameterized version is commented out on line 7). This value originates from req.body.searchText in routes/search.js (POST /search) and req.query.searchText in routes/api.js (GET /api/search), both unsanitized. An attacker can inject SQL via the search field, e.g. searchText=%' UNION SELECT username,password,3 FROM user-- to exfiltrate the user table or break out of the LIKE clause for data manipulation.

The Pug template uses the unescaped-output operator '!=' to render 'Search Results for: ' + searchText, where searchText is the raw, attacker-controlled value from req.body.searchText (routes/search.js POST /search) rendered via res.render('searchResult', ret). Because '!=' disables Pug's automatic HTML escaping, a payload like <script>alert(1)</script> submitted in the search form is reflected verbatim into the page, resulting in reflected XSS.

The error view renders error.stack directly into the response body. In app.js (lines 41-42), the stack is only suppressed when req.app.get('env') !== 'development', but NODE_ENV is never set to 'production' anywhere in this project (not in package.json scripts, Dockerfile, or docker-compose.yml), so Express defaults to 'development' and full stack traces (including file paths and internal module structure) are exposed to any client that triggers an error, e.g. by requesting a malformed URL.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The 'user' table stores the 'password' column as plain TEXT and rows are inserted with raw, unhashed password strings (e.g. 'S3cr37P@$$w0rD!', 'bad_password'). There is no hashing (bcrypt/scrypt/argon2) anywhere in the codebase before persistence, so a database compromise or the SQL injection in service/search.js would directly disclose every user's real password.

A hardcoded admin credential ('admin' / 'S3cr37P@$$w0rD!') is seeded directly in source code. If this seeding script is ever run against a real deployment (as opposed to a throwaway dev DB), the admin account password is fixed and recoverable from source control.

req.query (line 8) and the derived searchText value (line 9) are written to the server log via console.log() without sanitizing newlines or control characters. An attacker can inject CRLF sequences into the searchText query parameter to forge or split log entries, misleading log analysis/monitoring.

cwe: CWE-117: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs
